entry.name: TactAlign
entry.title: TactAlign: Human-to-Robot Policy Transfer via Tactile Alignment
entry.summary: Unpaired pivoting and insertion demonstrations from a human wearing the OSMO magnetic tactile glove (index-fingertip 3-axis signal) and from an Allegro hand with XELA 30-taxel fingertip sensors on a Franka arm, released as fingertip tactile, fingertip/wrist state, estimated object pose and actions at 10 Hz.
entry.hand: Human hand in the OSMO tactile glove; Wonik Allegro Hand (16 DoF) with XELA fingertip sensors on a Franka Emika Panda

sensor.note: Released per frame, one fingertip per modality. Human: observation/tactile (3, 1, 3) = the last 3 samples of one 3-axis OSMO reading on the index fingertip (finger column 'index' in every row), signed, near 0 at rest, peaks of ~200-1,500. Robot: observation/tactile (10, 30, 3) = 10 consecutive XELA samples (100 Hz) of one 30-taxel fingertip, 3 axes each. Frames are 0.1 s apart. Paper: glove recorded at 30 fps, XELA at 100 fps; glove baseline removed per trajectory, XELA baseline recorded per session. No force units.
sensor.maker: Meta FAIR (OSMO glove); XELA Robotics (robot fingertips)
sensor.model: OSMO tactile glove; XELA uSkin fingertip sensors (30 taxels each)

scale.text: Release: 210 human glove demonstrations (37,740 frames @10 Hz, ~63 min; pivoting 103 + insertion 98 + 9 val) and 104 robot episodes in the XELA encoder repo (9,876 frames, ~16.5 min, incl. one 300 s play episode); the two downstream robot repos (100 episodes) repeat the encoder repo's pivoting and insertion episodes. Paper: 200 human + 100 robot alignment demos, 140-160 human and 50 robot demos per co-training task (pivoting, insertion, lid closing), 20 human light-bulb demos

entry.access: Four ungated Hugging Face repos by the first author (youngw/tactile_align_encoder_pretrain_glove, _encoder_pretrain_xela, _downstream_insertion, _downstream_pivoting; 204 MB, Hugging Face datasets Arrow files with train/val splits), with no dataset card and no link from the paper or project page; the project page lists code as 'Coming Soon' and its data link is commented out.
caveats: Only pivoting and insertion are released; lid closing, light-bulb screwing (Manus glove + OSMO), the human-only-object demos, the force-labelled F/T dataset, play data for the glove, and all camera images are not in the repos.

One fingertip per sample: the glove repo carries only the index fingertip (one 3-axis reading), the robot repos one 30-taxel XELA fingertip; which Allegro finger is not stated (the paper's pivoting policy uses the index fingertip).

No images or depth: the RealSense D455 frames used for WiLoR hand pose and FoundationPose object pose are not released; observation/state and observation/object_pose are those estimates (human) or proprioception (robot).
No dataset card, README or license on any of the four repos; the arXiv paper is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and the project page CC BY-SA 4.0, neither covers the data.

Tactile values are baseline-subtracted magnetic readings without units; the paper takes the absolute value of the glove signal because the OSMO skin flips sign by quadrant, but the release keeps signed values.
Robot insertion episodes are 2.6-9.3 s and pivoting 5-15.6 s; robot demonstrations are kinesthetic teaching, not teleoperation.
The glove repo's metadata/info.json says fps 30 while its timestamps step by 0.1 s.

tracking.system: WiLoR (SAM3 hand masks) refined by ICP on FoundationStereo depth, Savitzky-Golay filtered
tracking.note: human fingertip positions and wrist pose from a RealSense D455 (images not released); released as observation/state (6,)

tracking.system: FoundationPose on FoundationStereo depth with SAM3/SAM3D meshes
tracking.note: observation/object_pose (6,) in both human and robot repos; some robot frames are all zero

tracking.system: Allegro joint position and effort (16 each)
Franka Emika Panda joint position and effort (7 each)
tracking.note: robot repos; demonstrations by kinesthetic teaching

other: Intel RealSense D455 recorded during collection; no images released
ATI Gamma F/T sensor for the force-labelled set (not released)
action / delta_action (6) and 32-step relative action chunks

sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.13579v1 (Sec. IV-A, IV-B, App. A, B-A, B-B, D, E)
https://yswi.github.io/tactalign/ (page text and HTML source: code link 'Coming Soon' to github.com/google/tactalign, commented-out data link)
unconfirmed: The HF repos are not linked from the paper or project page; they are attributed to the paper by uploader (full name 'youngsun wi', the first author), repo names and content (pivoting/insertion labels, OSMO 'index' finger rows, Allegro + Franka joints).

episodes=314 = 210 glove (201 train + 9 val) + 104 XELA encoder episodes (99 + 5); frames=47,616 = 37,740 + 9,876; hours=1.32 at the 0.1 s frame step. The downstream repos (insertion 49 + 3, pivoting 46 + 2 episodes) are left out because their episodes have the same lengths and peak values as encoder-repo episodes (e.g. downstream pivoting 27 = encoder 61, 156 frames, peak 2,230), i.e. they look like the same demonstrations.

The (3, 1, 3) glove array is a 3-step history window: slice i+1 of each row equals slice i of the next row. The (10, 30, 3) XELA array holds 10 distinct consecutive samples per frame (no overlap between rows), consistent with 100 fps XELA in 0.1 s frames.
XELA model: 30 taxels per fingertip matches XELA's curved Allegro fingertip (uSCu ALHA, 30 points); the paper says only 'Xela sensors mounted on the Allegro Hand fingertips'.
The paper's glove has 'three-axis magnetic tactile signals at the fingertips'; the OSMO glove has 12 taxels (5 fingertips + palm), but only the index fingertip is released.

objects: the alignment set uses one shared object per task (paper: Cheez-It box for pivoting, an adapter for insertion); whether the glove repo also holds human-only objects is not stated. Subjects not stated.
scenes=1: one Franka tabletop setup; not stated as a count.

download.per_episode: glove ~0.2 MB, robot ~0.6 MB on average (episodes are rows inside one Arrow file per split)
download.partial_fetch: none needed: each repo is one Arrow file per split; the whole release is 204 MB

sample.reason: Data download without login; no license or terms anywhere, so redistribution is not forbidden: re-host and label the collection 'License not stated'. The paper's CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and the project page's CC BY-SA 4.0 must not be shown as the data license.

episodes.why: Index-fingertip magnitude above rest + 100 for 15.8 s, peak 1,471; no NaN.
Longest contact among glove insertion episodes (31.8 s above rest + 100, peak 1,147).
Longest robot pivoting episode; max taxel-force norm above rest + 100 for 9.9 s, peak 2,230. Same demonstration as encoder repo episode 61.
Longest robot insertion episode in the release (all are 2.6-9.3 s); contact 6.9 s, peak 1,637.
The only play episode; contact above rest + 100 for 202.8 s over the episode, peak 10,935. Cut to 60 s.

sample.fetch_estimate: 0 MB more: all four repos' Arrow files (204 MB) were fetched for the survey (scratchpad s6/ta/). No video exists to re-host. Episode JSON: robot 60 s x 100 Hz x 90 values = 540k numbers for the play window; downsample to 10 Hz (the frame rate) or round to integers to stay under 2 MB.
sample.rules_applied: Tasks: 2 released tasks (pivoting, insertion), <= 6, so both taken. Episodes: with <= 3 tasks, 2-3 per task; here 2 per task, one human and one robot, to show both embodiments, plus the robot play episode (5 in total). Contact: magnitude above the episode's 5th percentile + 100 for >= 1 s, all channels present, no NaN. Length: glove 23-35 s and robot pivoting 15.6 s kept whole; play cut to 60 s.
deviations: Robot insertion episode is 9.3 s, below 10 s: every robot insertion episode in the release is 2.6-9.3 s.
No camera video: the release has no images, so the viewer shows touch and state only.
